words: ولا تطع منهم آثما أو كفورا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waw could forbid obedience to both together while allowing separate obedience; aw makes clear that none of the named people should be obeyed.
rows.anchor: واو بليغة في هذا المعنى لأنك إذا قلت لا تطع زيدا وعمرا فجائز أن يكون نهيتني عن طاعتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibitions punished Israel for killing prophets, taking usury, and wrongfully consuming people’s property, paralleling 4:160.
rows.anchor: حرمنا ذلك عليهم عقوبة لهم بقتلهم الأنبياء وأخذهم الربا واستحلالهم أموال الناس بالباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative gloss takes their wrongdoing as prohibited acts by which they wronged themselves.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بغيهم ظلمهم على أنفسهم في ارتكابهم المحظورات

rows.speaker: علي بن إبراهيم
rows.claim: ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm says Israelite rulers deprived the poor of fowl and fat, so God prohibited those foods because of their oppression.
rows.anchor: كانوا يمنعون فقراءهم من أكل لحوم الطير والشحوم فحرم الله ذلك ببغيهم على فقرائهم ذكره علي بن إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though obligations serve a benefit and expose people to reward, this prohibition is called punishment because their grave sin required changing the benefit; lesser guilt would not have required it.
rows.anchor: ويسأل فيقال كيف يكون التكليف عقوبة وهو تابع للمصلحة وتعريض للثواب وجوابه إنه إنما سمي جزاء وعقابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is truthful about the prohibition, their wrongdoing, and everything; it punished earlier generations and benefited later ones until abrogation.
rows.anchor: أي في الإخبار عن التحريم وعن بغيهم وفي كل شيء وفي أن ذلك التحريم عقوبة لأوائلهم ومصلحة لمن بعدهم إلى وقت النسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they reject Muhammad, he should cite God’s vast mercy: He delays punishment, but no one can repel it at its appointed time; criminals are deniers.
rows.anchor: أي لا يدفع عذابه إذا جاء وقته

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Adam and Eve patched themselves with leaves from Paradise, specifically fig leaves, until they resembled clothing.
rows.anchor: حتى صار كهيئة الثوب عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their expulsion served a divine benefit, not punishment, since prophets do not deserve punishment; the commentary discussed this in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: لأن المصلحة اقتضت إخراجهما من الجنة وإهباطهما إلى الأرض لا على وجه العقوبة فإن الأنبياء لا يستحقون العقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tilkuma addresses two people; the kāf is the marker of direct address.
rows.anchor: لكنه لما خاطب اثنين قال تلكما والكاف حرف الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s address recalls His prohibition and rebukes Adam and Eve for what they did.
rows.anchor: لما عاتبهما الله سبحانه ووبخهما على ارتكاب المنهي عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their self-wronging means they deprived themselves of reward by leaving what was recommended; ẓulm means diminution.
rows.anchor: ومعناه بخسناها الثواب بترك المندوب إليه فالظلم هو النقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who allow minor sins and think they reduce the sinner’s reward can gloss self-wronging as loss of reward.
rows.anchor: ومن ذهب إلى أنهم فعلا صغيرة فإنه يحمل الظلم على تنقيص الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who say a minor sin is expiated without reducing reward cannot accept that gloss and, on their account, the verse has no benefit under it.
rows.anchor: فأما من قال إن الصغيرة تقع مكفرة من غير أن تنقص من ثواب فاعلها شيئا فلا يتصور هذا المعنى عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam and Eve did not deserve punishment; people of high religious standing regret even a slight lapse more intensely.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف أن حواء وآدم لم يستحقا العقاب وإنما قالا ذلك لأن من جل في الدين قدمه كثر على يسير الزلل ندمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss says they wronged themselves by descending to earth and losing their comfortable life.
rows.anchor: ظلمنا أنفسنا بالنزول إلى الأرض ومفارقة العيش الرغد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maghfira means covering, as explained earlier in the commentary.
rows.anchor: معناه وإن لم تستر علينا لأن المغفرة هي الستر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask God to favor them with the gift that completes the reward they forfeited, along with other forms of grace.
rows.anchor: أي ولم تتفضل علينا بنعمتك التي يتم بها ما فوتناه على نفوسنا من الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The losers are those who lose and make no gain.
rows.anchor: أي من جملة من خسر ولم يربح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person may wrong himself by causing undeserved harm without repelling greater harm or gaining a commensurate benefit, but cannot punish himself.
rows.anchor: والإنسان يصح أن يظلم نفسه بأن يدخل عليها ضررا غير مستحق فلا يدفع عنها ضررا أعظم منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descent and enmity statement was explained earlier in the commentary on al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: قد مر تفسيره في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People live and die on earth and will be raised from it at the resurrection.
rows.anchor: عند البعث يوم القيامة قال الجبائي:

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī argues that resurrection is from this same earth; afterward God destroys it and moves people by a blast to another earth called al-Sāhira, citing 79:14.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي: في الآية دلالة على أن الله سبحانه يخرج العباد يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī cites 79:14 for his account that the resurrected are moved to the land called al-Sāhira.
rows.anchor: فإذا هم بالساهرة [النازعات: 14]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ reads maʿdhiratan with accusative; the other readers use nominative.
rows.anchor: القراءة: قرأ حفص معذرة بالنصب والباقون بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nominative means “our admonition is an excuse,” with an omitted subject; accusative means “we apologize.” Sibawayh gives the same accusative construction.
rows.anchor: من قرأ معذرة بالرفع فتقديره موعظتنا معذرة فيكون خبر مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: شهر بن حوشب وأبو نهيك
rows.claim: A noncanonical reading by Shahr b. Ḥawshab and Abū Nuhayk has yaʿdūn, understood as yaʿtadūn with tāʾ assimilated into dāl.
rows.anchor: عن شهر بن حوشب وأبي نهيك يعدون عن الحسن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan’s variant has ḍamma on yāʾ and means entering the Sabbath, like entering a month or Friday.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن يسبتون بضم الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa on yāʾ, the reading means performing and observing the Sabbath; sabata-yasbutu means to honor it.
rows.anchor: ومن فتح الياء أراد يفعلون السبت ويقيمون عمل يوم السبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥītān is the plural of ḥūt; Arabs most often call fish ḥītān or nīnān.
rows.anchor: حيتان جمع حوت وأكثر ما يسمى العرب السمك الحيتان والنينان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAdā means to transgress and exceed a limit; its root sense is going beyond bounds.
rows.anchor: وعدا فلان يعدو عدوانا وعداء وعدوا وعدوا ظلم وأصله مجاوزة الحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sharaʿa originally means appearing; shariʿa and shurʿa are visible riverbanks, and a ship’s sail is named for being exposed.
rows.anchor: والشرع أصله الظهور ومنه الشرعة والشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿdhira and related ʿudhr terms name an excuse; al-muʿdhir has a valid excuse, while al-muʿadhdhir pretends to have one and is negligent.
rows.anchor: والمعذرة والعذر والعذرى والعذرة واحد مصدر عذرته أعذره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muʿtadhir can describe someone with or without an excuse; man yaʿdhurunī asks who will uphold his excuse.
rows.anchor: والمعتذر يقال لمن له عذر ولمن لا عذر له وقولهم من يعذرني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first idh is accusative as the time about which the Prophet is told to ask; idh at the fish’s arrival is likewise accusative.
rows.anchor: إذ يعدون موضع إذ نصب على معنى سلهم عن عدوهم أي عن وقت ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuraʿan is an accusative circumstantial qualifier of the fish.
rows.anchor: شرعا نصب على الحال من الحيتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred parse makes the kāf in kadhālika accusative under nablu; alternatively it modifies the fish’s arrival and nablu begins a new clause.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول أجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lam taʿiẓūn is originally limā; the alif drops after a preposition, as in mim, fīm, ʿalām, and ʿam.
rows.anchor: أصله لما ولكن هذه الألف تحذف مع حرف الجر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the seaside town as Eylah.
rows.anchor: وهي إيلة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās identifies it as Midian.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي مدين عنه أيضا

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī identifies the town as Tiberias.
rows.anchor: وقيل: طبرية عن الزهري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They transgressed by fishing on the Sabbath and exceeding its limits.
rows.anchor: أي يظلمون فيه بصيد السمك ويتجاوزون الحد في أمر السبت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the fish appeared on the surface of the water.
rows.anchor: ظاهرة على وجه الماء عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the fish came in succession.
rows.anchor: وقيل: متتابعة عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the fish raised their heads and came to the doors like white rams because they felt safe.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: كانت تشرع إلى أبوابها مثل الكباش البيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On days when they did not observe the Sabbath, the fish submerged and did not appear.
rows.anchor: أي ويوم لا يكون السبت كانت تغوص في الماء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One account says they channeled the fish into pools from which they could not escape and caught them on Sunday.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية عكرمة عن ابن عباس اتخذوا الحياض فكانوا يسوقون الحيتان إليها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says they caught fish and took them by hand on the Sabbath.
rows.anchor: تناولوها باليد في يوم السبت عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tested them with a severe trial because of their disobedience.
rows.anchor: مثل ذلك الاختبار الشديد نختبرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the fish did not come on non-Sabbath days in the same conspicuous way; “We test them” then starts a new clause.
rows.anchor: وعلى المعنى الآخر لا تأتيهم الحيتان مثل ذلك الإتيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people divided into fishers, silent observers, and admonishers; the silent group addressed the admonishers.
rows.anchor: وكانوا ثلاث فرق فرقة قانصة وفرقة ساكتة وفرقة واعظة

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says the silent group asked from despair that sinners would accept admonition; commanding right is obligatory only while acceptance is not hopeless.
rows.anchor: عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They expected God to destroy the people in this world for disobedience or punish them severely in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: والله مهلكهم في الدنيا بمعصيتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The admonishers say their warning discharges their duty to God in forbidding wrongdoing, so God cannot ask why they failed to warn.
rows.anchor: معناه موعظتنا إياهم معذرة إلى الله وتأدية لفرضه في النهي عن المنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also admonish in hope that the people will become God-fearing and return.
rows.anchor: بالوعظ: { يتقون } ويرجعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Medinese read bīs without hamza; Ibn ʿĀmir reads biʾs; Abū Bakr (not Ḥammād) reads bayiʾs; the rest read baʾīs.
rows.anchor: القراءة: قرأ أهل المدينة بعذاب بيس بكسر الباء غير مهموز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noncanonical readings include bayiʾs from Ibn ʿAbbās; biʾs from Zayd b. Thābit, Yaḥyā, al-Sulamī, and al-Ḥasan; bīs from Ṭalḥa and reportedly Nāfiʿ; bāʾis from Mujāhid.
rows.anchor: وروي في الشواذ عن ابن عباس بيئس على وزن فيعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʾīs can be an adjective on faʿīl from bāʾusa, meaning severe, or a maṣdar used adjectivally, as in al-nadhīr and al-nakīr.
rows.anchor: من قرأ بئيس فإنه يحتمل أمرين أن يكون فعيلا من بؤس يبؤس إذا كان شديد البأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The biʾs reading treats the normally verbal form as a noun and adjective, like qīl and qāl.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ بعذاب بئس فإنه جعل بئس الذي هو فعل اسما فوصف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayyiʾs is analyzed as fayʿal, analogous to ḍaygham and ḥaydar; this pattern is normally for a weak second radical, so this form is judged an error.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز كسر العين منه لأن فيعل بناء اختص به ما كان عينه ياء أو واوا

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinnī explains the hamza in the variant by its resemblance to the two weak letters.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني: وإنما جاء في الهمز لمشابهتها حرفي العلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biʾs on faʿl may suggest biʾsa al-rajulu baʾsatan, “the man was courageous,” implying punishment came promptly; it may instead be shortened from baʾīs.
rows.anchor: وأما بئس على فعل فإنه جاء على بئس الرجل بأسة إذا شجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bīs is explained as a softened hamza in biʾs, moved toward yāʾ; Ibn Mayyāda illustrates the softened pronunciation of yawmaʾidhin.
rows.anchor: وأما بيس في وزن جيش فكأنه أراد بئس فخفف الهمزة

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abū Ḥātim rejects al-Ḥasan’s biʾs reading, arguing it would require mā after it, as in niʿma mā.
rows.anchor: وأنكر أبو حاتم قراءة الحسن بئس

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abū Zayd distinguishes bāʾusa for being mighty or brave from biʾsa in poverty; baʾsāʾ is a noun for hardship or poverty.
rows.anchor: قال أبو زيد: يقال بؤس الرجل يبؤس بأسا إذا كان شديد البأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAtā is rebellion into the gravest sins; ʿātī is deeply disobedient, and a ʿātī night is very dark.
rows.anchor: والعتو الخروج إلى أفحش الذنوب والعاتي المبالغ في المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khāsiʾ means driven away and kept from good, from the verb for driving a dog away.
rows.anchor: والخاسىء المطرود المبعد عن الخير من خسأت الكلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They abandoned the admonition and continued fishing; God rescued those forbidding evil and punished the wrongdoers for disobedience.
rows.anchor: فلما ترك أهل هذه القرية ما ذكرهم الواعظون به ولم ينتهوا عن ارتكاب المعصية

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says the severe punishment struck them before they were transformed into apes.
rows.anchor: وذلك العذاب لحقهم قبل أن مسخوا قردة عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says the admonishers and silent observers were saved while the fishers perished.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أن نجت الفرقتان وهلكت الثالثة وبه قال السدي

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the fishers and silent group perished and only the admonishers were saved; this is also related from Abū ʿAbd Allāh.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أنه هلكت الفرقتان ونجت الفرقة الناهية وبه قال ابن زيد

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima reports Ibn ʿAbbās suspending judgment about the silent group; al-Jubbāʾī chooses this restraint.
rows.anchor: والثالث: التوقي فيه روي عن عكرمة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the third group was saved because warning with a threat is the strongest admonition and they did warn; killing a believer is graver than eating fish.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: إنه نجا الفرقة الثالثة لأنه ليس شيء أبلغ في الأمر بالمعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They persisted in corruption and defied the prohibition rather than abandon the sin.
rows.anchor: لم يتركوا ما نهوا عنه وتمردوا في الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made them apes; the imperative “be” shows that nothing can thwart His power.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكر كن ليدل على أنه سبحانه لا يمتنع عليه شيء

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj allows that they heard the command as speech, an account also attributed to Abū al-Hudhayl and said to make the punishment more striking.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الزجاج أن يكون قيل لهم ذلك بكلام سمعوه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says they became tailed apes that howled after having been men and women.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: صاروا قردة لها أذناب تعاوي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they remained apes for three days, then died without descendants; no metamorphosis lasted longer than three days.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال ولم يمكث مسخ فوق ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says they lived seven days and then died.
rows.anchor: عاشوا سبعة أيام ثم ماتوا عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says they reproduced, but the author rejects this as implausible because apes, like dogs, are not descendants of Adam’s children.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن وليس بالوجه لأن من المعلوم أن القردة ليست من أولاد آدم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports the Prophet saying God never transformed a creature and gave it offspring or descendants.
rows.anchor: ووردت الرواية عن ابن مسعود قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An account places the story in David’s time.
rows.anchor: القصة: قيل كانت هذه القصة في زمن داود ع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they were commanded to observe Friday but chose Saturday, when fishing was forbidden; abundant white, plump fish appeared on its surface.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس قال: أمروا باليوم الذي أمرتم به يوم الجمعة فتركوه واختاروا يوم السبت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In Ibn ʿAbbās’s account, Satan suggested channeling fish into pools and nets on Saturday, then taking them Sunday.
rows.anchor: ثم أتاهم الشيطان وقال إنما نهيتهم عن أخذها يوم السبت فاتخذوا الحياض والشبكات

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says a man tied a fish to shore and took and roasted it Sunday; when no punishment came, others copied him, ate and sold fish, and numbered about twelve thousand.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن زيد قال أخذ رجل منهم حوتا وربط في ذنبه خيطا وشده إلى الساحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The admonishers separated from the others and would not live with them; one morning no offender emerged, and the others found them transformed.
rows.anchor: فاعتزلتهم الفرقة الناهية ولم تساكنهم فأصبحوا يوما ولم يخرج من العاصية أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apes recognized their former companions but were not recognized in return; they wept and nodded yes when asked whether they had been warned.
rows.anchor: فكانت القردة تعرفهم وهم لا يعرفونها فجعلت تبكي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the young became apes and the old became pigs.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: صارت الشبان قردة والشيوخ خنازير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Bakr reads yumsikūn with still mīm; other readers use open mīm and geminated sīn, with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: القراءة: قرأ أبو بكر يمسكون بتسكين الميم والباقون

rows.speaker: السلمي
rows.claim: Al-Sulamī’s noncanonical wādārasū is from tadārasū with assimilation.
rows.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة السلمي وادارسوا ما فيه أراد تدارسوا فأدغم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj distinguishes khalaf, a generation following another, from khulf, what replaces something lost.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: يقال للقرن الذي يجيء في أثر قرن خلف

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ uses khalaf ṣidq for a good successor and khalaf sūʾ for a bad one; fatḥ is more often used for praise.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: يقال هو خلف صدق وخلف سوء

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: ʿAlī b. ʿĪsā says khalaf and khulf can substitute for one another.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن عيسى: وقد يوضع أحدهما مكان الآخر

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labīd’s verse uses khalaf for a disfavored successor generation, comparing them to mange-ridden skin.
rows.anchor: ذهب الذين يعاش في أكنافهم وبقيت في خلف كجلد الأجرب

rows.speaker: حسان
rows.claim: Ḥassān’s verse uses khalaf for followers of earlier people in obedience to God.
rows.anchor: لنا القدم الأولى إليك وخلفنا لأولنا في طاعة الله تابع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAraḍ is a transient thing with little duration; the philosophical term for an accident follows from its impermanence beside bodies.
rows.anchor: والعرض ما يعرض ويقل لبثه ومنه سمي العرض القائم بالجسم عرضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dars is repetition: rereading a book or repeated rain and wind erasing a house’s trace.
rows.anchor: والدرس تكرير الشيء ويقال درس الكتاب إذا كرر قراءته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amsaka, masaka, tamassaka, and istamsaka all mean to hold fast to something.
rows.anchor: وأمسك ومسك وتمسك واستمسك بالشيء بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaʾkhudhūna ʿaraḍa is a circumstantial accusative; wariṯū al-kitāb describes khalaf, and darasū is conjoined to wariṯū.
rows.anchor: يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى في موضع النصب على الحال من الضمير في ورثوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant clause through illā al-ḥaqq is parenthetical between wariṯū and darasū; there is no pause before mā fīhi.
rows.anchor: اعتراض بين ورثوا ودرسوا ولا يجوز الوقف من أول الآية إلا على قوله ما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predicate of alladhīna yumsikūn is innā lā nuḍīʿu ajra al-muṣliḥīn, with minhum omitted as context supplies it.
rows.anchor: فحذف منهم لدلالة الكلام عليه كما في قوله السمن منوان بدرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means “We do not waste their reward” because they reform; or the predicate is omitted and the reason stands for the result.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون التقدير لا نضيع أجرهم لأن المصلحين هم الذين يمسكون بالكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse turns from earlier generations to successors; inheriting the Book means inheriting the Torah.
rows.anchor: معناه فذهب أولئك وقام مقامهم قوم آخرون ورثوا الكتاب يعني التوراة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says worldly goods are present enjoyment consumed by both righteous and wicked people.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس يقال الدنيا عرض حاضر يأكل منه البر والفاجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says they took bribes and issued unjust judgments; another says they took bribes but judged rightly; either way it was paltry gain.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنهم كانوا يرتشون ويحكمون بجور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-adnā may mean immediate gain or this low, transient world.
rows.anchor: وأراد بقوله هذا الأدنى هذا العاجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim of forgiveness exposes greed and persistence: they take whatever appears, lawful or unlawful, while presuming God will forgive.
rows.anchor: وهذا إخبار عن حرصهم على الدنيا وإصرارهم على الذنوب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd b. Jubayr, and Mujāhid say they take a later unlawful bribe and treat it as lawful, showing persistence.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه وإن جاءهم حرام من الرشوة وغيرها بعد ذلك أخذوه

words: مِيثَٰقَ الْكِتَٰبِ أَن لَّا يَقُولُوا۟ عَلَى اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْحَقَّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The judges had covenanted in the Torah not to lie about God or attribute anything beyond what He revealed to Moses; it promises no forgiveness while sin persists.
rows.anchor: معناه ألم يؤخذ على هؤلاء المرتشين في الأحكام القائلين سيغفر لنا إذا عوتبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One gloss says they read the Torah and remembered its contents.
rows.anchor: أي وقرؤوا ما فيه فهم ذاكرون لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, darasū is conjoined to wariṯū: they inherited and studied the Book but neglected and failed to act on it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه معطوف على قوله ورثوا الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife’s reward for people who obey God is better for those avoiding His disobedience.
rows.anchor: ما أعده الله لأوليائه في الدار الآخرة من النعيم والثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With yāʾ, the question asks whether this group understands; with tāʾ, Muhammad is told to ask them whether they understand.
rows.anchor: من قرأ بالياء فمعناه أفلا يعقل هذه الطائفة

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Ibn Zayd say the Book is the Torah, which its adherents preserve without altering or concealing.
rows.anchor: أي لا يحرفونه ولا يكتمونه عن مجاهد وابن زيد

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ identifies the Book as the Qurʾān and its adherents as Muḥammad’s community.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الكتاب القرآن والمتمسك به أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم عن عطاء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says no amount of gain satisfies them.
rows.anchor: لا يشبعهم شيء عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is singled out because of its high rank or especially strong obligation.
rows.anchor: إنما خص الصلاة بالذكر لجلالة موقعها أو شدة تأكدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not waste reformers’ reward but recompenses their work as they deserve.
rows.anchor: أي لا نضيع جزاء عملهم ونثيبهم على ما يستحقونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Basrans, Ibn Kathīr, and al-Kisāʾī read ṭayf without alif, as do al-Nakhaʿī and al-Aswad b. Zayd; the others read ṭāʾif with alif.
rows.anchor: القراءة: قرأ أهل البصرة وابن كثير والكسائي طيف بغير ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Medinese read yumiddūnahum with ḍamma yāʾ and kasra mīm; others use fatḥa yāʾ and ḍamma mīm; al-Jaḥdarī has yumādūnahum and ʿĪsā b. ʿUmar yuqṣirūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة يمدونهم بضم الياء وكسر الميم والباقون بفتح الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭayf is the verbal noun for a dream apparition visiting someone, hence a passing thought; ṭāʾif has the same sense, like khāṭir, though ṭayf is more common.
rows.anchor: الطيف مصدر طاف الخيال يطيف طيفا إذا ألم به في المنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The line about ṭayf al-khayāl witnesses a phantom; al-Aʿshā’s verse uses ṭāʾif for a jinn visitation.
rows.anchor: وقال الأعشى: وتصبح عن غب السرى وكأنما ألم بها من طائف الجن أولق

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī prefers the majority’s open-yāʾ reading: favorable Qurʾānic contexts use amdadtu while unfavorable ones use maddadtu; he explains the other reading by analogy with bashshirhum.
rows.anchor: فهذا يدل على أن الوجه فتح الياء كما ذهب إليه الأكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yumādūnahum is the reciprocal form of madda and means they assist them.
rows.anchor: ويمادونهم يفاعلونهم منه أي يعاونونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqṣurūn is a dialect form of aqṣara or qaṣara: the former means desist by choice, the latter be unable.
rows.anchor: وقصر يقصر لغة في أقصر يقصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mamsūs can mean someone touched by jinn; of water, it means water touched by hands.
rows.anchor: الممسوس الذي به مس جن والممسوس من المياه ما نالته الأيدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ijtibāʾ is extracting or selecting something for oneself, parallel to iṣṭifāʾ; its root sense includes extraction or gathering water.
rows.anchor: والاجتباء افتعال من الجباية ونظيره الاصطفاء

rows.speaker: الفراء وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says ijtabaytu al-kalām means making up speech spontaneously; Abū ʿUbayda gives “invented it.”
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: اجتبيت الكلام واختلقته وارتجلته

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abū Zayd says these expressions describe speech begun without preparation.
rows.anchor: قال أبو زيد هذه الحروف تقولها العرب للكلام يبتدؤه الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baṣāʾir are proofs and arguments, plural of baṣīra; they can also mean blood tracks.
rows.anchor: والبصائر البراهين والحجج جمع بصيرة والبصائر أيضا طرائق الدم

rows.speaker: الأشعر الجعفي
rows.claim: Al-Ashʿar al-Juʿfī introduces a verse using baṣāʾir for traces carried on shoulders, illustrating the sense of tracks.
rows.anchor: قال الأشعر الجعفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation of al-Ashʿar al-Juʿfī’s quoted verse uses baṣāʾir for tracks carried on shoulders.
rows.anchor: راحوا بصائرهم على أكتافهم وبصيرتي يعدو بها عتد وأى

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Baṣāʾir can also mean shields; al-Zajjāj says these senses share the idea of appearance and clarity.
rows.anchor: أو البصيرة الترس وجمعها بصائر قال الزجاج: وجميع هذا معناه ظهور الشيء وتبيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first idh is temporal and takes a response like a conditional; the second is locative and marks sudden appearance.
rows.anchor: الإعراب: إذا الأولى ظرف زمان ويكون لها جواب بمنزلة الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pious are those who avoid disobedience to God.
rows.anchor: { إن الذين اتقوا } الله باجتناب معاصيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Suddī say Satan whispers and tempts them toward sin; they recall its punishment and desist.
rows.anchor: قيل معناه إذا وسوس إليهم الشيطان وأغراهم بمعصيته

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains this as Satan circling them with whispers.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: يعني إذا طاف عليهم الشيطان بوساوسه

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد
rows.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr and Mujāhid say it describes someone who gets angry, remembers God, and restrains his anger.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: هو الرجل الذي يغضب الغضبة فيتذكر فيكظم غيظه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid also says it is someone intending a sin who remembers God and abandons it.
rows.anchor: وروي عنه أيضا أنه قال هو الرجل يهم بالذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say ṭāʾif means anger and ṭayf means madness; another view treats them as synonymous.
rows.anchor: وقيل: طائف غضب وطيف جنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They then see the right path clearly.
rows.anchor: { فإذا هم مبصرون } للرشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists’ brothers, devils among jinn and humans, increase their error and disobedience and make their conduct attractive.
rows.anchor: معناه وإخوان المشركين من شياطين الجن والإنس يمدونهم في الضلال

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda say the devils do not stop leading people astray or show them mercy.
rows.anchor: ثم لا يكفون يعني الشيطان عن استغوائهم ولا يرحمونهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي والجبائي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Suddī, and al-Jubbāʾī say unbelievers are the devils’ brothers: devils lead them astray, and unbelievers do not desist as the pious do.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه وإخوان الشياطين من الكفار يمدهم الشياطين في الغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss makes the devils the ones who never stop seducing them or restraining them from indecency.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه ثم لا يقصر الشياطين عن إغوائهم

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد والزجاج
rows.claim: Qatāda, Mujāhid, and al-Zajjāj say that when Muhammad brings a sign they deny it; when he delays one, they ask why he has not produced it himself.
rows.anchor: فليس كل ما تقوله وحي من السماء عن قتادة ومجاهد والزجاج

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والجبائي وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Jubbāʾī, and Abū Muslim say they demanded a proposed sign and asked why Muhammad had not chosen it and requested it from God.
rows.anchor: فتسأل ربك أن يأتيك بها عن ابن عباس والجبائي وأبي مسلم

words: إِنَّمَا أَتَّبِعُ مَا يُوحَىٰ إِلَيَّ مِن رَّبِّي
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad follows revelation; God manifests signs when He knows they serve a benefit, and the Prophet may not request them without permission.
rows.anchor: أي لست آتي بالآيات من عندي وإنما يفعلها الله تعالى ويظهرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that the Prophet’s words and deeds follow revelation; he may not act by opinion or analogy.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أن أفعال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأقواله تابعة للوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān gives clear proofs from God that let people see religious matters; it is guidance and a blessing in religion and worldly life.
rows.anchor: هذا القرآن دلائل ظاهرة وحجج واضحة وبراهين ساطعة من ربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are singled out because they benefit from the proofs and guidance, unlike unbelievers.
rows.anchor: خص المؤمنين بالذكر لأنهم المنتفعون بها دون غيرهم من الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The excerpt begins an anonymous coherence note saying this verse connects to an earlier statement, but cuts off before identifying it.
rows.anchor: النظم: قيل إن هذه الآية اتصلت بقوله
